turns.speaker: Baleki
turns.text: That trunk has collected an embarrassing amount of dust.

turns.speaker: Cemvi
turns.text: Ha, at least it won't be spotless for long.

turns.speaker: Baleki
turns.text: Could we leave before dawn to reach Avren Pass while the roads are quiet?

notes.text: Baleki suggested leaving before dawn to reach Avren Pass while the roads are quiet.

turns.speaker: Cemvi
turns.text: I can't leave before dawn; I'm on the night shift the day before.

notes.text: Cemvi cannot leave before dawn because Cemvi works the night shift the day before.

turns.speaker: Baleki
turns.text: Then let's stay overnight in Belmere and cross Avren Pass in daylight.

notes.text: Baleki suggested staying overnight in Belmere and crossing Avren Pass in daylight.

turns.speaker: Cemvi
turns.text: That works; I booked a room in Belmere for Saturday night.

notes.text: Cemvi booked a room in Belmere for Saturday night after Baleki suggested staying there.

turns.speaker: Baleki
turns.text: My fingers are cold just thinking about unpacking.

turns.speaker: Cemvi
turns.text: Actually, my shift got swapped, so I can leave before dawn after all.

notes.text: Cemvi can now leave before dawn because the night shift was swapped.

turns.speaker: Baleki
turns.text: Good, that makes the daylight crossing easier.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep thinking about a tiny mending booth in the covered arcade at Nuvessa. I can sew hems and replace zippers, but I don't know where to begin.

notes.text: The user is considering a mending booth in the covered arcade at Nuvessa and can sew hems and replace zippers.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Start with a one-day trial and list your three most common fixes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I have about 900 crowns saved for setup, and I want to test it at the autumn market before signing a lease.

notes.text: The user has about 900 crowns saved for setup and plans to test the mending booth at the autumn market before signing a lease.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That keeps the commitment small. What repairs do people request most?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don't know whether people will laugh if my sign is hand-painted, honestly. It's a very small sign.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A hand-painted sign fits a neighborhood mending booth just fine.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly hems and trousers, but people ask for darning too and I actually enjoy it. My neighbor Dazri handles market table bookings and said there's an opening on 12 October; I'll ask tonight, but my machine jams if I rush.

notes.text: The user enjoys darning and receives frequent requests for it.
Dazri handles market table bookings and said an opening is available on 12 October.
The user plans to ask Dazri about the opening tonight.
The user's sewing machine jams when rushed.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Keep the opening list focused, and get the machine checked before opening.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, that's a relief. I feel less tangled now.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good. You have a sensible first step.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm trying to start a mobile bike-repair cart in Orelun. I can put in 1,400 crowns, but I really don't want a loan.

notes.text: The user can invest 1,400 crowns in a mobile bike-repair cart in Orelun and does not want a loan.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That gives you a clear ceiling. Have you sketched out a route?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: First I pictured weekend pop-ups, but now weekday pickup seems better; lots of riders at the ferry yard finish late.

notes.text: The user is now leaning toward weekday pickup after first considering weekend pop-ups because many riders at the ferry yard finish late.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That sounds promising. What tools do you already have?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, the gear list is making my head spin; I'll check the closet before I say what I own.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Start with what you own. What repairs would you offer first?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Would 12 crowns for a flat fix sound silly? The old garage by Lumei charged that, but I could include pickup.

notes.text: The user is considering 12 crowns as the flat-fix price with pickup, based on the old garage's rate at Lumei.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Price the parts and time too; pickup can justify a little more.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll try 15 crowns then, with pickup inside the east loop only. If I get three bookings a week for a month, I'll buy a folding stand.

notes.text: The user plans to charge 15 crowns for flat fixes with pickup inside the east loop.
The user plans to buy a folding stand after getting three bookings a week for a month.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That is a clear test. Track time, parts, and repeat requests.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to start a little tea-blending business from my flat in Soremi, mostly mint and roasted barley.

notes.text: The user wants to start a tea-blending business in Soremi featuring mint and roasted barley.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: What do you want to test first: the blends or the packaging?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My friend Fareni offered the back room at her studio for a Saturday tasting in June; I haven't said yes yet.

notes.text: Fareni offered the user the studio's back room for a Saturday tasting in June, and the user has not accepted.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A tasting is a useful test. What packaging are you considering?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm leaning toward paper sachets because glass jars feel fancy but the shipping cost adds up. Does that seem sensible?

notes.text: The user is leaning toward paper sachets because glass jars increase shipping costs.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Compare a small batch of both before ordering much.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, I checked courier rates today and changed my mind on jars; I can source reused ones locally through Delu's refill stall.

notes.text: After leaning toward paper sachets, the user now favors reused jars sourced locally through Delu's refill stall.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Local reused jars sound workable. Check the cleaning rules, too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Could I do a sampler of three tiny blends for 8 crowns? I still need to calculate the ingredient cost before deciding.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Run the ingredient math first; three samples can be a tidy test.

turns.speaker: Deya
turns.text: The lease on the tiny kitchen in Avelu came through this morning, so the bun pop-up can finally happen.

notes.text: Deya said the tiny kitchen lease in Avelu came through this morning for a bun pop-up.

turns.speaker: Emon
turns.text: I can cover the first flour order, but only up to 240 crowns. The quote came in lower than I feared.

notes.text: Emon can cover up to 240 crowns for the first flour order.

turns.speaker: Deya
turns.text: That'll cover us. My test buns were too sweet, so I'm cutting the glaze by half for the next batch on Thursday.

notes.text: Deya plans to cut the glaze by half for the next bun batch on Thursday.

turns.speaker: Emon
turns.text: The savory rolls were better, and the neighbors asked if we could keep those every week.

notes.text: Emon preferred the savory rolls and said neighbors asked for savory rolls every week.

turns.speaker: Deya
turns.text: Wait, did you reserve the warm shelf, or am I mixing up the message from the kiln people?

turns.speaker: Emon
turns.text: I did; Ederi at the equipment co-op held the warm shelf for us until 14 July.

notes.text: Emon said Ederi at the equipment co-op held the warm shelf until 14 July.

turns.speaker: Deya
turns.text: Great, I was worried we were going to bake at home again. I found a stack of little paper bags in the cupboard.

turns.speaker: Emon
turns.text: Keep those for samples; I want the first menu to be sesame buns and the savory rolls.

notes.text: Emon wants sesame buns and savory rolls on the first menu.

turns.speaker: Deya
turns.text: Sounds good. I painted a small sign teal yesterday, though the letters are wonky. I'll redo it before the test table.

notes.text: Deya made a small teal sign yesterday and plans to redo the lettering before the test table.

turns.speaker: Emon
turns.text: I'll bring a ruler, and if it's pouring we can move the sign under the awning.

turns.speaker: Eshvi
turns.text: I handed in my notice at the dye house on Monday; the custom scarf idea is starting to feel real.

notes.text: Eshvi handed in a notice at the dye house on Monday and feels the custom scarf idea is becoming real.

turns.speaker: Fadren
turns.text: That's a big move. The rent for that workroom by Naref is 310 crowns a month, right?

turns.speaker: Eshvi
turns.text: It was 310, but Dazem called yesterday and offered the smaller room for 260 if I sign for six months.

notes.text: Eshvi said Dazem offered a smaller workroom for 260 crowns per month if Eshvi signs for six months, down from 310 crowns.

turns.speaker: Fadren
turns.text: I'd take it. You can wait for custom dye orders before buying the second vat; the shared one at our studio is free on Saturdays.

notes.text: Fadren suggested that Eshvi wait for custom dye orders before buying a second vat and said the shared studio vat is free on Saturdays.

turns.speaker: Eshvi
turns.text: I used to think I needed a full palette at launch, but after the market last week I only want to start with indigo and rust.

notes.text: After the market last week, Eshvi wanted to start with indigo and rust instead of a full palette.

turns.speaker: Fadren
turns.text: That'll keep the first batch manageable, and those two shades photographed best anyway.

turns.speaker: Eshvi
turns.text: Can you send me the name of the label printer you used? I remember it was near Tovek but the shop name escaped me.

turns.speaker: Fadren
turns.text: It's Elaru Print Room on Savel Lane, beside the old cistern; they quoted 46 crowns for fifty labels.

notes.text: Fadren said Elaru Print Room on Savel Lane quoted 46 crowns for fifty labels.

turns.speaker: Eshvi
turns.text: Perfect, I'll email Elaru Print Room after lunch and ask for matte stock; glossy labels looked tacky on my sample.

notes.text: Eshvi plans to email Elaru Print Room after lunch about matte stock because Eshvi disliked the glossy sample.

turns.speaker: Fadren
turns.text: I'll bring the cloth swatches tomorrow, and we can choose the two shades by the window.

notes.text: Fadren plans to bring cloth swatches tomorrow so Fadren and Eshvi can choose two shades.

turns.speaker: Farun
turns.text: I found a secondhand soup cart in Fenori, and the owner says the boiler still holds heat.

notes.text: Farun found a secondhand soup cart in Fenori, and the owner said the boiler still holds heat.

turns.speaker: Delo
turns.text: Did you see it run? Last time a seller said that and the burner sputtered out in five minutes.

turns.speaker: Farun
turns.text: Yeah, I tested it for half an hour yesterday. The wheel squeaks, though, so I'll ask for 180 crowns instead of 230.

notes.text: Farun tested the cart for half an hour yesterday.
Farun plans to offer 180 crowns for the cart because a wheel squeaks, down from the seller's 230-crown asking price.

turns.speaker: Delo
turns.text: Fair. Are you still planning to sell near the tram garden, or did the steward turn down the permit?

turns.speaker: Farun
turns.text: The steward approved a trial spot for two Sundays in September, but said no open flame; the boiler is electric.

notes.text: Farun said a steward approved a trial selling spot for two Sundays in September and prohibited open flames.
Farun said the cart's boiler is electric.

turns.speaker: Delo
turns.text: Electric works then. I'd keep the first menu to lentil soup and flatbread, since the bowl storage is tight.

notes.text: Delo suggested limiting Farun's first menu to lentil soup and flatbread because bowl storage is tight.

turns.speaker: Farun
turns.text: I was thinking three soups before, but you're right, I'll start with two and add one only if people ask.

notes.text: Farun changed the planned opening menu from three soups to two, with a third only if customers ask.

turns.speaker: Delo
turns.text: I can make a chalkboard for you. I'm free Sunday after my shift if you bring the wood panel.

notes.text: Delo offered to make Farun a chalkboard and said Delo is free Sunday after Delo's shift if Farun brings a wood panel.

turns.speaker: Farun
turns.text: Deal, I'll bring the panel. I finally got the borrowed canopy back from Eder yesterday, so we can shade the bowls.

notes.text: Farun plans to bring a wood panel Sunday after Delo's shift.
Farun got the borrowed canopy back from Eder yesterday.

turns.speaker: Delo
turns.text: I'll text you a sketch tonight, and let's hope the sign stays upright in the breeze.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey, can you help me organize this week? My brain is soup.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Of course. What's due first?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Anatomy is Thursday, stats is the following Monday, and cramming after work just isn't sticking.

notes.text: The user has anatomy on Thursday.
The user has stats the following Monday and says cramming after work is not sticking.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: When do you focus best?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Before lunch, hands down. I can do 40 minutes before my shift if my phone's in the kitchen, otherwise I definately check it.

notes.text: The user focuses best before lunch and can study for 40 minutes before a shift with the phone in the kitchen.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That sounds like a good anchor.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I used to study at the library, but the ferry closure means the Neralin reading room near my flat is easier now. Also keep Sunday mostly clear, I'm visiting my aunt.

notes.text: The user used to study at the library and now finds the Neralin reading room near home easier because the ferry is closed.
The user plans to visit an aunt on Sunday and wants Sunday mostly clear.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Want a simple plan through Monday?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Please, a simple one would be great.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sure. Two short stats blocks, then review.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I got my old anatomy cards out of the tote, so I'll review them on the bus.

notes.text: The user found old anatomy cards and plans to review them on the bus.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Nice. Bus review can stay low pressure.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Could you help me practice for an oral exam? I freeze when the questions come quickly, it's embarassing.

notes.text: The user freezes when oral exam questions come quickly.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: We can go one question at a time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hesra says the big clock behind the panel makes her lose her place, so I'd rather not see a timer either.

notes.text: The user said Hesra loses her place when the clock behind the exam panel is visible.
The user prefers practice without a visible timer.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: I can keep time quietly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes, do eight questions with a two-second pause after each; that would feel manageable.

notes.text: The user accepted quiet timing and wants eight questions with a two-second pause after each.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Done. No timer on screen.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I passed the mock last May, but I blanked on the first question anyway.

notes.text: The user passed a mock exam last May but blanked on the first question.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: One rough start doesn't erase the pass.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The real oral is in June. I'm going to record myself this weekend and listen once on the tram.

notes.text: The user's oral exam is in June.
The user plans to record themself this weekend and listen to the recording on the tram.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Want to try a warm-up question now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One sec, I'm making tea first because the kettle's gone feral again lol.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Take your time. I'll start easy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you help me map out exam day? I've never made a revision schedule that works.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sure, which papers and when?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Design history in the morning and stats at four, both finals on the same day.

notes.text: The user has a design history final in the morning and a stats final at four on the same day.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Try one subject per block, with a proper break.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The campus greenhouse is usually my best spot, but it's closed until Wednesday for repairs.

notes.text: The user usually prefers studying in the campus greenhouse, which is closed for repairs until Wednesday.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Could use the tiled hall by the east stairwell.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That hall gets loud after lunch, and the echo triggers my migraines.

notes.text: The user says the tiled hall gets loud after lunch and echo triggers the user's migraines.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Right, skip that one. Sorry.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The institute opened the Solvi Annex last spring, and its upper floor is usually empty by two.

notes.text: The user says the institute opened the Solvi Annex last spring and its upper floor is usually empty by two.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That sounds like a quieter option.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, breakfast first. That should work.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good, use the early block for design history.

turns.speaker: Gireya
turns.text: Your entrance exam is next Tuesday, right? You looked like you were living in that practice room.

turns.speaker: Hovren
turns.text: Yep, next Tuesday, but I finally booked the nook at Pelorin Hall for three evenings.

notes.text: Hovren confirmed the entrance exam is next Tuesday and booked the nook at Pelorin Hall for three evenings.

turns.speaker: Gireya
turns.text: I've got my chemistry practical on Friday, and the glass pipettes make me nervous for no reason lol.

notes.text: Gireya has a chemistry practical on Friday and feels nervous about glass pipettes.

turns.speaker: Hovren
turns.text: You've got this. I could quiz you on labels if that'd help.

turns.speaker: Gireya
turns.text: Please do, but only after my shift; I'm rostered at the Junel Bend café tomorrow.

notes.text: Gireya asked Hovren to quiz her after her shift and said she is rostered at the Junel Bend café tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Hovren
turns.text: I'll bring the paper cards, it'll be easier than shouting over ovens.

notes.text: Hovren plans to bring paper cards to quiz Gireya after her shift.

turns.speaker: Gireya
turns.text: Actually, they moved me to closing, so lunch is free now. Could we meet at the pump steps before work instead? probly easier.

notes.text: Gireya said her shift was moved to closing, leaving lunch free, and proposed meeting at the pump steps before work.

turns.speaker: Hovren
turns.text: Perfect, same time then.

turns.speaker: Gireya
turns.text: I used to use flashcards on my phone, but the screen gives me headaches lately, so paper is best.

notes.text: Gireya used to study with flashcards on her phone but now prefers paper because the screen gives her headaches.

turns.speaker: Hovren
turns.text: Got it, paper it is.

turns.speaker: Gireya
turns.text: Thanks! I got the seat near the window last time and nobody came through.

notes.text: Gireya said nobody came through when she sat near a window last time.

turns.speaker: Hovren
turns.text: Keep it. I'll see you at the pump steps tomorrow.

notes.text: Hovren plans to meet Gireya at the pump steps tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Ilven
turns.text: Are you still aiming for the geology retake in October? You said the first score didn't reflect what you knew.

turns.speaker: Ghanor
turns.text: Yeah, I registered yesterday. I'd been waiting to see whether the lab section in Meren Cove had space.

notes.text: Ghanor registered for the geology retake yesterday after waiting to see if the Meren Cove lab section had space.

turns.speaker: Ilven
turns.text: It does, but now it meets at seven, which could be rough if you're taking the ferry from Rilven Quay.

notes.text: Ilven said the Meren Cove lab section now meets at seven and could be difficult for Ghanor if Ghanor takes the ferry from Rilven Quay.

turns.speaker: Ghanor
turns.text: I do take the ferry, and my aunt can lend me her old scooter through October if I pass the road test.

notes.text: Ghanor said Ghanor takes the ferry from Rilven Quay and may borrow an aunt's scooter through October if Ghanor passes the road test.

turns.speaker: Ilven
turns.text: That might change things. You passed the road test this morning, you texted me the photo.

notes.text: Ilven said Ghanor passed the road test this morning.

turns.speaker: Ghanor
turns.text: I did! They gave me the temporary slip; the card comes later.

notes.text: Ghanor confirmed passing the road test and said Ghanor received a temporary slip while the card will arrive later.

turns.speaker: Ilven
turns.text: Ahh, that's lucky timing.

turns.speaker: Ghanor
turns.text: I don't like riding unfamiliar routes after dark anyway; I can travel in daylight on Saturdays, the only day I don't work.

notes.text: Ghanor avoids unfamiliar routes after dark and is free to travel in daylight on Saturdays.

turns.speaker: Ilven
turns.text: I work Saturday mornings too, but Sunday is clear for both of us.

notes.text: Ilven said Ilven works Saturday mornings and Sunday is clear for both of them.

turns.speaker: Ghanor
turns.text: Cool, let's do Sunday then. I'll carry the sample map so we can mark the route.

notes.text: Ghanor and Ilven plan to go Sunday, and Ghanor will bring a sample map to mark the route.

turns.speaker: Ilven
turns.text: Good. I switched from morning flashcards to audio notes in August, and I remember more on the ferry now.

notes.text: Ilven switched from morning flashcards to audio notes in August and remembers more on the ferry now.

turns.speaker: Ghanor
turns.text: Could you send me your audio setup? My lecture notes are a mess of half sentences.

turns.speaker: Hivana
turns.text: How are you holding up? Your code oral is Wednesday and the written paper's Friday, right?

turns.speaker: Irenel
turns.text: Yes, and I'm still deciding whether to stay at Bivra House or take the late bus back.

notes.text: Irenel has a code oral on Wednesday and a written exam on Friday, and has not decided whether to stay at Bivra House or take the late bus.

turns.speaker: Hivana
turns.text: You can stay at my place if you want; I live by Teren Slip and the tram runs until ten.

notes.text: Hivana offered Irenel a place to stay near Teren Slip and said the tram runs until ten.

turns.speaker: Irenel
turns.text: That's kind. I didn't want to impose, but I forgot the last bus was at nine.

notes.text: Irenel said the last bus was at nine.

turns.speaker: Hivana
turns.text: My exams are done now, so I can leave the spare mattress made up until Friday.

notes.text: Hivana said Hivana's exams are done and the spare mattress can stay made up until Friday.

turns.speaker: Irenel
turns.text: Wait, yours were the ones in May? I thought the term ended this week.

turns.speaker: Hivana
turns.text: They were moved up two weeks ago; I've been free since Monday.

notes.text: Hivana said the exams were moved up two weeks ago and Hivana has been free since Monday.

turns.speaker: Irenel
turns.text: Ahh, that explains the offer. I can stay over tonight, then head back after the oral on Wednesday.

notes.text: Irenel plans to stay at Hivana's place tonight and head back after the code oral on Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Hivana
turns.text: Sure. I started doing one timed outline before lunch, and the first exam felt less scary.

notes.text: Hivana started doing one timed outline before lunch, which made Hivana's first exam feel less scary.

turns.speaker: Irenel
turns.text: I'll try that tomorrow. I normally freeze if I see a blank page, so a rough outline sounds doable.

notes.text: Irenel plans to try a timed outline tomorrow and usually freezes at a blank page.

turns.speaker: Hivana
turns.text: I used to write full paragraphs right away, but I've switched to bullet skeletons since May.

notes.text: Hivana switched from writing full paragraphs to bullet skeletons since May.

turns.speaker: Irenel
turns.text: If I pass, I'm buying myself a mango bun. If I fail, well, twelve mango buns.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Could you help me get ready for the neighborhood fair?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sure, what's settled so far?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm running a tea-and-spice table at the Keldin Row fair on June 17; they moved it from the 10th because the school yard's booked.

notes.text: The user is running a tea-and-spice table at the Keldin Row fair.
The user said the Keldin Row fair was moved from the 10th to June 17 because the school yard was booked.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Got it. What else is settled?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I need a quiet corner near the table for anyone who needs a break.

notes.text: The user wants a quiet corner near the tea-and-spice table for anyone needing a break.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Makes sense. What supplies are missing?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Two folding tables; Kelmira said she can lend one, so I need to borrow one more.

notes.text: The user said Kelmira can lend one folding table, leaving one more table to borrow.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: I'll keep one more table on the list.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Citron-mint tea sold out before noon last year, so I plan to brew twice as much this time.

notes.text: The user said citron-mint tea sold out before noon last year.
The user plans to brew twice as much citron-mint tea this time.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Any setup detail you'd like me to remember?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'd like my tea-and-spice table on the shaded side; strong sun makes the spice labels peel.

notes.text: The user wants the tea-and-spice table on the shaded side because strong sun makes the spice labels peel.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Shaded spot, got it. I'll add that.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The Brindle Fen fair added a children's bike loop, and I'm worried it crosses the food line.

notes.text: The user is worried the Brindle Fen fair's children's bike loop crosses the food line.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Where does it meet the food stalls?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: At the west gate, beside Luyani's dumpling queue. Luyani offered to move the cart ten meters if we mark a new cable path.

notes.text: The user said the bike loop meets the food line beside Luyani's dumpling queue at the west gate.
The user said Luyani offered to move the dumpling cart ten meters if organizers mark a new cable path.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Have you settled on route markers?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Chalk washed off in a drizzle last time, so I want reusable blue cones this year; I found twelve in the rec-room closet.

notes.text: The user said chalk markers washed off in a drizzle last time.

turns.text: Yeah, a pallet sat behind a closed gate, so I called the driver, got a new slot, and told dispatch before it became a missed pickup.

notes.text: Ruzhen handled a delayed pallet by calling the driver, getting a new slot, and telling dispatch.

turns.speaker: Pireva
turns.text: Was that the one you fixed by updating the dock sheet in August?

turns.speaker: Ruzhen
turns.text: No, separate thing. The dock sheet change was in August; this time the gate was locked.

notes.text: Ruzhen said the locked-gate pallet incident was separate from the dock-sheet change in August.

turns.speaker: Pireva
turns.text: Got it, I always mix those stories up; you said last week your interview nerves were mostly about salary.

notes.text: Pireva said Ruzhen's interview nerves had mostly concerned salary last week.

turns.speaker: Ruzhen
turns.text: Not now, honestly. I told them my target is 74k and I'd consider a lower base for paid training; I emailed a thank-you before lunch.

notes.text: Ruzhen said salary was no longer the main source of interview nerves.
Ruzhen's salary target is 74k, with flexibility for paid training.
Ruzhen emailed a thank-you before lunch.

turns.speaker: Pireva
turns.text: Nice. Did they say when a decision comes?

turns.speaker: Ruzhen
turns.text: The hiring lead said they'd decide by Wednesday, and I can do one Saturday a month, but every weekend would clash with my ceramics stall.

notes.text: The hiring lead said the decision would come by Wednesday.
Ruzhen can work one Saturday a month but not every weekend because of the ceramics stall.

turns.speaker: Pireva
turns.text: That seems fair. Are you still okay with the longer bus ride to Veyru?

turns.speaker: Ruzhen
turns.text: The bus is fine if the shift ends by six. I'll wait for the decision before planning anything.

notes.text: Ruzhen is comfortable with the bus ride to Veyru if the shift ends by six.
Ruzhen plans to wait for the hiring decision before making plans.

turns.speaker: Sorevi
turns.text: Did your second interview at the glass workshop in Pashun happen yesterday?

turns.speaker: Parun
turns.text: Yeah, I met operations lead Pashari, and they asked how I'd handle a missed kiln check.

notes.text: Parun met operations lead Pashari at a second interview at the glass workshop in Pashun yesterday.
Pashari asked Parun how Parun would handle a missed kiln check.

turns.speaker: Sorevi
turns.text: You told me last month you didn't want shift supervision. Has that changed?

notes.text: Sorevi said Parun did not want shift supervision last month.

turns.speaker: Parun
turns.text: A little: I'd supervise two people, but not take the whole night roster. I asked if weekends rotate.

notes.text: Parun is open to supervising two people but not taking the full night roster.
Parun asked whether the role rotates weekends.

turns.speaker: Sorevi
turns.text: What example did you use for the missed check?

turns.speaker: Parun
turns.text: The alarm at the Sorev kiln was muted during maintenance, so I added a sign-off box to the paper log.

notes.text: Parun added a sign-off box to the paper log after the Sorev kiln alarm was muted during maintenance.

turns.speaker: Sorevi
turns.text: That was your idea, right? I remember you saying the old log had no initials line.

notes.text: Sorevi remembered Parun saying the old paper log lacked an initials line.

turns.speaker: Parun
turns.text: Right. I sent a thank-you before lunch and asked if they need references; they already have my supervisor's number.

notes.text: Parun sent a thank-you before lunch.
Parun asked whether the workshop needed references, and the workshop already had Parun's supervisor's number.

turns.speaker: Sorevi
turns.text: If they call this week, will you take it if the pay is the same?

turns.speaker: Parun
turns.text: If the schedule stays in the posted range, yes; the pay is fine but my commute from Rivathi is already long.

notes.text: Parun would accept the role if the schedule remains in the posted range.
Parun considers the pay acceptable but says the commute from Rivathi is already long.

turns.speaker: Sorevi
turns.text: I know you like the workshop floor more than admin, though.

notes.text: Sorevi said Parun prefers workshop-floor work to administrative work.

turns.speaker: Parun
turns.text: I do; paperwork all day drains me. I'll wait on the call; the hiring lead told me no later than Wednesday.

notes.text: Parun prefers workshop-floor work to paperwork.
The hiring lead told Parun to expect a decision no later than Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Prusali
turns.text: How'd the interview go at the archive cooperative in Relun? You were waiting ages to hear back.

turns.speaker: Senvor
turns.text: It was fine, but they asked me to demonstrate the inventory app on a tablet and the test file wouldn't load.

notes.text: The archive cooperative asked Senvor to demonstrate an inventory app on a tablet, but the test file failed to load.

turns.speaker: Prusali
turns.text: Did they give you a paper backup or just watch you sweat?

turns.speaker: Senvor
turns.text: They handed me printed records, and I matched 18 folders before the timer ended.

notes.text: Senvor matched 18 folders from printed records before the timer ended.

turns.speaker: Prusali
turns.text: You'd been practicing that sorting script since spring, right?

notes.text: Prusali said Senvor had practiced a sorting script since spring.

turns.speaker: Senvor
turns.text: Yeah, although the test was manual. I told panelist Sarev I'd rather check a small batch carefully than race and misfile.

notes.text: Senvor told panelist Sarev that Senvor would rather check a small batch carefully than risk misfiling.

turns.speaker: Prusali
turns.text: That fits you. Do you still prefer a quieter office over the public desk?

notes.text: Prusali said Senvor prefers a quieter office over the public desk.

turns.speaker: Senvor
turns.text: Definitely, and I asked if the quiet room can be used for cataloguing. They said onboarding starts in two weeks if I get the offer.

notes.text: Senvor prefers a quieter office to the public desk.
Senvor asked whether the quiet room could be used for cataloguing.
The cooperative said onboarding would start in two weeks if Senvor received the offer.

turns.speaker: Prusali
turns.text: You got a follow-up already?

turns.speaker: Senvor
turns.text: A note came this morning asking for two references; I sent them both, and I'm relieved they didn't ask for another timed test.

notes.text: Senvor received a request for two references this morning and sent both references.
Senvor felt relieved that the cooperative did not ask for another timed test.

turns.speaker: Prusali
turns.text: Nice, are you thinking you'll take it if they offer?

turns.speaker: Senvor
turns.text: I think so, if the hours are still 9 to 5. I don't want to commute to Relun for split shifts.

notes.text: Senvor is inclined to accept the role if the hours remain 9 to 5.
Senvor does not want to commute to Relun for split shifts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey, I'm doing the craft market at Vellum Quay this weekend. Still deciding what to bring.

notes.text: The user plans to sell at the craft market at Vellum Quay this weekend.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: What are you thinking of bringing?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly hand-dyed linen napkins in rust and indigo; I like simple block patterns.

notes.text: The user plans to bring hand-dyed linen napkins in rust and indigo and prefers simple block patterns.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That palette sounds great on linen.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep second-guessing the tablecloth, probly spent an hour unfolding the same two lol.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Maybe a plain cream cloth will let the colors pop.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good call, I'll sew little weights into the corners so the wind can't flip it.

notes.text: The user plans to sew small weights into the tablecloth corners to keep the cloth from blowing over.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That should keep the setup tidy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I used to print plastic labels, but since spring I've switched to recycled cotton tags.

notes.text: The user switched from plastic labels to recycled cotton tags since spring.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Those should fit the linen look nicely.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: If I say the table is 'blue and rust', maybe that sounds like a paint store haha.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Maybe try 'indigo linens and rust-dyed details'.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I got a spot at the craft market in Teralune Hall, and they invited me to do a little pottery demo.

notes.text: The user got a spot at the Teralune Hall craft market and was invited to give a pottery demo.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: What will you make for the demo?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Tiny pinch pots; I like demos people can finish in five minutes.

notes.text: The user likes pottery demos that visitors can finish in five minutes.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a friendly format for a busy aisle.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I was folding the flyer while cooking and somehow tore it in half lol.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: At least the demo itself should be less messy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We tried a long demo last year and people drifted off, so I'm keeping this one short.

notes.text: The user said people drifted off during a long demo last year.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Five minutes sounds much easier to browse into.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don't use the stamp kit anymore; I switched to carving initials by hand in May.

notes.text: The user stopped using the stamp kit and switched to carving initials by hand in May.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That'll make each pot feel personal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll pack extra clay for Saturday if the weather holds; any tip for keeping it damp?

notes.text: The user plans to pack extra clay for Saturday if the weather holds.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A sealed tub with a damp cloth should do it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I finally got a spot at the Tovari craft market; first time selling woven reed baskets!

notes.text: The user got a spot at the Tovari craft market to sell woven reed baskets for the first time.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congrats! How are you pricing them?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Small ones at 18, larger ones at 32; I want the prices accessible without ignoring the hours.

notes.text: The user plans to price small baskets at 18 and larger baskets at 32 and wants prices to reflect the work while staying accessible.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A size card could make that clear.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Taviri thinks the opening rush will be over by noon.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Worth having plenty ready near the front.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Last year I accepted custom orders and got swamped; this time I'm selling ready-made only.

notes.text: The user plans to sell only ready-made baskets at the Tovari craft market this time after getting swamped by custom orders last year.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That should keep your day manageable.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you help me write a small sign?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sure: 'Handwoven baskets, ready to take home.'

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Love that, I'll use 'ready to take home' on the sign.

notes.text: The user plans to use the wording 'ready to take home' on the sign.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That'll read clearly from the aisle.

turns.speaker: Weyra
turns.text: Are you still in for the craft market at Nivelle Yard next month?

turns.speaker: Tavik
turns.text: Definitely, I've been dyeing cotton cord for it every evening.

notes.text: Tavik has been dyeing cotton cord for the Nivelle Yard craft market every evening.

turns.speaker: Weyra
turns.text: I booked us two tables yesterday, so there's room for the pegboard and your trays.

notes.text: Weyra booked two tables for the Nivelle Yard craft market yesterday.

turns.speaker: Tavik
turns.text: Oh good, that's more space than I expected.

turns.speaker: Weyra
turns.text: Can you bring the pegboard and hooks from your shed?

turns.speaker: Tavik
turns.text: Yep, I'll bring them; the last frame was too wobbly without hooks.

notes.text: Tavik plans to bring the pegboard and hooks from Tavik's shed.

turns.speaker: Weyra
turns.text: I switched to handwritten price cards after the ink smudged in the rain last time.

notes.text: Weyra switched to handwritten price cards after ink smudged in the rain last time.

turns.speaker: Tavik
turns.text: Good call, I forget little stuff when setup gets hectic.

turns.speaker: Weyra
turns.text: At the last market, the little woven coasters sold out before lunch.

notes.text: Weyra said the little woven coasters sold out before lunch at the last market.

turns.speaker: Tavik
turns.text: I'll put the cord bundles at eye level this time; they got missed last market.

notes.text: Tavik plans to display the cord bundles at eye level after the bundles were missed at the last market.

turns.speaker: Weyra
turns.text: Let's get there by 7:30 for setup and try for the end spot.

notes.text: Weyra plans to arrive by 7:30 for setup and try for the end spot.

turns.speaker: Tavik
turns.text: Works for me, I'll pack a thermos too.

notes.text: Tavik plans to pack a thermos for the 7:30 setup.

turns.speaker: Vohani
turns.text: The craft market got moved inside to the Neralin Arcade because of the rain, right?

turns.speaker: Wema
turns.text: Yeah, the organizers moved it indoors; I recieved Tavish's vendor map this morning.

notes.text: Wema confirmed the craft market moved indoors to Neralin Arcade because of rain and said Tavish's vendor map arrived this morning.

turns.speaker: Vohani
turns.text: I got assigned row B; my pressed-flower frames don't do well in direct sun anyway.

notes.text: Vohani was assigned row B and said Vohani's pressed-flower frames do not do well in direct sun.

turns.speaker: Wema
turns.text: Nice, I can swap my table with you if they put me by a window.

turns.speaker: Vohani
turns.text: I used to sell loose dried stems, but since October I've bundled them with little paper sleeves.

notes.text: Vohani switched from selling loose dried stems to bundling stems in small paper sleeves since October.

turns.speaker: Wema
turns.text: Those look tidier on a table too.

notes.text: Wema thinks the paper sleeves make Vohani's dried stems look tidier on a table.

turns.speaker: Vohani
turns.text: Tavish says the aisle opens at 9, so I want to unload before then.

notes.text: Vohani said Tavish stated that the aisle opens at 9, and Vohani plans to unload before opening.

turns.speaker: Wema
turns.text: I can come early and help you carry the frames from the loading bay.

notes.text: Wema offered to help Vohani carry the frames from the loading bay.

turns.speaker: Vohani
turns.text: That'd be great, my wrist is fine now but the crates are awkward.

turns.speaker: Wema
turns.text: I'll bring the padded cart I used at the spring market; it folds flat.

notes.text: Wema plans to bring the padded cart used at the spring market, and the cart folds flat.

turns.speaker: Vohani
turns.text: Perfect, I'll pack the frames in the blue crate before I leave.

notes.text: Vohani plans to pack the frames in the blue crate before leaving.

turns.speaker: Wema
turns.text: Send me a text when you're ready downstairs.

turns.speaker: Teyu
turns.text: How's prep for the craft market at Waveth Fen going?

turns.speaker: Vireli
turns.text: Pretty good, I'm bringing glass bead wind chimes and a small repair kit.

notes.text: Vireli plans to bring glass bead wind chimes and a small repair kit to the craft market.

turns.speaker: Teyu
turns.text: I reserved the covered corner by the water barrel yesterday; my paper lanterns can't handle drizzle.

notes.text: Teyu reserved the covered corner by the water barrel yesterday and said paper lanterns cannot handle drizzle.

turns.speaker: Vireli
turns.text: Smart, last time the breeze took two of mine across the field.

notes.text: Vireli said a breeze carried two of Vireli's wind chimes across the field last time.

turns.speaker: Teyu
turns.text: Since my wrist healed in March, I've switched from huge lanterns to smaller folded ones.

notes.text: Teyu switched from huge lanterns to smaller folded lanterns after Teyu's wrist healed in March.

turns.speaker: Vireli
turns.text: Those sound easier to pack, and they'll still glow nicely.

turns.speaker: Teyu
turns.text: Would you be able to help me clip the canopy at setup?

turns.speaker: Vireli
turns.text: Sure, I can bring the extra clamps from my workshop.

notes.text: Vireli offered to bring extra clamps from Vireli's workshop to help Teyu clip the canopy.

turns.speaker: Teyu
turns.text: Still staring at the price tags for the tiny lanterns and making no progress, ugh.

turns.speaker: Vireli
turns.text: At the spring market, I priced my small chimes at 12, and shoppers bought them as gifts.

notes.text: Vireli priced Vireli's small chimes at 12 at the spring market, and shoppers bought the chimes as gifts.

turns.speaker: Teyu
turns.text: I'll try 10 for the tiny lanterns and bring a few extras; let's meet at 7:15, since the market opens at 8.

notes.text: Teyu plans to price the tiny lanterns at 10, bring extras, and meet Vireli at 7:15 before the market opens at 8.

turns.speaker: Vireli
turns.text: Works, I'll leave from my place at 6:45 and pick you up.

notes.text: Vireli plans to leave from Vireli's place at 6:45 and pick up Teyu.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yaveli and I are hoping to fish next Saturday; crowded launches stress me out, so I'd rather stay on the bank. Can you help me pick a quiet spot?

notes.text: The user plans to fish with Yaveli next Saturday.
The user prefers bank fishing and finds crowded launches stressful.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sure. Do you already have a place in mind?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yaveli keeps suggesting Cloudmere Spill's gravel bank; she says she caught perch there in April. I only know it's outside Larkettle.

notes.text: The user is considering Cloudmere Spill's gravel bank after Yaveli recommended it.
The user said Yaveli caught perch at Cloudmere Spill in April.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That sounds promising. I can help you make a simple day-trip list.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes, please keep it light. I have a small tackle pouch and hate hauling extra gear.

notes.text: The user prefers a light fishing kit and dislikes hauling extra gear.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Pack your rod, a small tackle pouch, water, a snack, and a light rain layer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I pack three kinds of crackers every single time. At this point it's a bit ridiculous, lol.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Three kinds of crackers sounds like a solid tradition.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yaveli can drive, and she offered to bring folding stools; I'll fill my thermos with mint tea.

notes.text: The user said Yaveli can drive to the fishing trip.
Yaveli offered to bring folding stools.
The user plans to bring mint tea in a thermos.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That covers the ride and a place to sit. Want a short checklist?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, correction: Yaveli's reel is the one with the cracked handle, not mine. I'll lend her my spare.

notes.text: Yaveli's reel has the cracked handle.
The user plans to lend Yaveli a spare reel.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Got it—your spare reel is for Yaveli.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Zorvi and I are heading to Brindlecoil Fen at dawn tomorrow. He's bringing fly gear; I still feel more confident with a spinning rod.

notes.text: The user plans to fish at Brindlecoil Fen with Zorvi at dawn tomorrow.
The user prefers using a spinning rod over fly gear.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Are you hoping to target anything specific there?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Avenor at the little boat hut said there are trout in the eastern run, so I want to try that before the sun gets high.

notes.text: The user said Avenor reported trout in the eastern run at Brindlecoil Fen.
The user plans to try the eastern run before the sun gets high.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sounds like a good first stop. Want a shore-fishing checklist?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yep, compact please. I don't want to carry a net unless we really need it.

notes.text: The user prefers a compact kit and would rather not carry a net.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Small tackle box, forceps, water, and a light layer should cover the basics.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The alarm's already set; if I turn it off half-asleep, that's on me.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Maybe leave your phone across the room so you have to get up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I lost my old headlamp during the last trip, so I'll use the clip light from my bag.

notes.text: The user lost an old headlamp during the last trip and plans to use a clip light from the bag.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That should keep your hands free.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh wait, Zorvi just messaged that the gate opens at 6, not 5:30. We'll aim to arrive at 6.

notes.text: The user said Zorvi messaged that the gate opens at 6.
The user and Zorvi plan to arrive at 6.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good catch; six should give you time to get settled.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm planning a two-night fishing trip with Zefari for the first weekend in May. The canoe makes me nervous; I'd rather use the walking trail and fish from shore.

notes.text: The user plans a two-night fishing trip with Zefari for the first weekend in May.
The user prefers walking to a shore-fishing spot over using a canoe.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Where did you settle on going?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Lanternmoss Bend, about three hours from home. I've camped there once, but never fished there.

notes.text: The user and Zefari chose Lanternmoss Bend for the fishing trip.
The user has camped at Lanternmoss Bend once but has never fished there.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Want to start with food, campsite gear, or fishing tackle?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Food. I don't eat meat, and Zefari is happy with beans and rice as long as there's hot sauce.

notes.text: The user does not eat meat.
The user said Zefari likes beans and rice with hot sauce.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Beans, rice, hot sauce, and a few vegetables make an easy one-pot meal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Nice, that solves one part of it.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Great. Have you two sorted out cooking gear yet?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Zefari said she can borrow a two-burner stove from Arelun, but I only have one fuel canister.

notes.text: The user reported that Zefari said she can borrow a two-burner stove from Arelun.
The user has one fuel canister.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Check whether the stove needs one or two canisters, and I can help build a list.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Update: Arelun dropped the stove off this morning, and we found a second canister in the garage, so gear's covered.

notes.text: Arelun dropped off the two-burner stove this morning.
The user and Zefari found a second fuel canister in the garage.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Nice, one big piece of camp setup is settled.

turns.speaker: Yorali
turns.text: I found the old route to Kettlewax Canal. We could walk from the north gate and fish by the footbridge.

notes.text: Yorali suggested walking from Kettlewax Canal's north gate to fish by the footbridge.

turns.speaker: Zimel
turns.text: That was the stretch with loose gravel, right? I don't want to repeat my ankle slip.

notes.text: Zimel asked whether the Kettlewax Canal stretch had loose gravel and said an earlier ankle slip was not something Zimel wanted to repeat.

turns.speaker: Yorali
turns.text: Yeah, same stretch. I can bring walking poles; the path is less muddy after lunch.

notes.text: Yorali offered to bring walking poles.
Yorali said the path is less muddy after lunch.

turns.speaker: Zimel
turns.text: Oh, that's why you suggested going later. Saturday after lunch works, and I'll bring my old wading boots just in case.

notes.text: Zimel agreed to go Saturday after lunch.
Zimel planned to bring old wading boots.

turns.speaker: Yorali
turns.text: I'll grab my small folding stool too; it packs flat.

notes.text: Yorali plans to bring a small folding stool.

turns.speaker: Zimel
turns.text: Actually, I stopped wading after the boot seam split last autumn, so I'll stay on the bank.

notes.text: Zimel stopped wading after a boot seam split last autumn.
Zimel plans to stay on the bank.

turns.speaker: Yorali
turns.text: Fair enough. Any bait you'd like me to grab?

turns.speaker: Zimel
turns.text: Corn and bread; trout ignored the bright lures last time.

notes.text: Zimel plans to use corn and bread as bait.
Zimel said trout ignored bright lures last time.

turns.speaker: Yorali
turns.text: My box has hooks for both, so we're set.

turns.speaker: Zimel
turns.text: Great. Do you still have the green-handled nippers I left at your place? Could you bring them?

notes.text: Zimel asked Yorali to bring green-handled nippers that Zimel said were left at Yorali's place.

turns.speaker: Yorali
turns.text: Found them in my tackle drawer this morning; I'll put them by the door.

notes.text: Yorali found the green-handled nippers in the tackle drawer this morning.
Yorali plans to put the nippers by the door.

turns.speaker: Zimel
turns.text: Perfect, coffee's on me. I'm done with bright lures for good anyway.

notes.text: Zimel is done using bright lures.

turns.speaker: Arelun
turns.text: I was at Glassheron Pool last month, and the waterline was much lower than I expected.

notes.text: Arelun said the waterline at Glassheron Pool was much lower than expected last month.

turns.speaker: Yavren
turns.text: Then let's switch to Siltwhistle Cove. The casting deck there is easier on my wrist.

notes.text: Yavren proposed moving the trip to Siltwhistle Cove because the casting deck is easier on Yavren's wrist.

turns.speaker: Arelun
turns.text: Works for me. Are we still taking the little boat or fishing from the bank?

turns.speaker: Yavren
turns.text: Bank. I don't trust that boat after the oarlock came loose last spring.

notes.text: Yavren chose bank fishing because the boat's oarlock came loose last spring.

turns.speaker: Arelun

notes.text: Eltan's bike was soaked at the station in August, the chain rusted, and Eltan paid $70 for a replacement.

turns.speaker: Dazhi
turns.text: I keep a small repair kit in my locker now after two similar mishaps.

notes.text: Dazhi keeps a small repair kit in a locker after two similar mishaps.

turns.speaker: Eltan
turns.text: I might start doing that; right now all I carry is a snack and a bad attitude.

notes.text: Eltan is considering keeping a repair kit in a locker and currently carries a snack.

turns.speaker: Dazhi
turns.text: The snack is non-negotiable though; long rides make me feral.

turns.speaker: Eltan
turns.text: Same, especially when the feeder bus is late. It was 25 minutes behind yesterday, so I ate two snacks.

notes.text: Eltan's feeder bus ran 25 minutes late yesterday, and Eltan ate two snacks during the delay.

turns.speaker: Eshven
turns.text: I started taking the 5:50 ferry from Valedune to Nacre Point in October, and door to door is still almost two hours.

notes.text: Eshven started taking the 5:50 ferry from Valedune to Nacre Point in October, and the commute takes almost two hours door to door.

turns.speaker: Cirelle
turns.text: Oof, that early ferry sounds miserable; I don't know how you do that before sunrise.

turns.speaker: Eshven
turns.text: The ferry is packed now; before the new shift pattern, I could usually get a seat.

notes.text: Eshven says the 5:50 ferry is packed now, while Eshven could usually get a seat before the new shift pattern.

turns.speaker: Cirelle
turns.text: Did the shift pattern change last month?

turns.speaker: Eshven
turns.text: Yeah, the dock crew moved from 7 to 6:30 in December, so the ferry fills earlier.

notes.text: Eshven said the dock crew moved its start time from 7 to 6:30 in December, which made the ferry fill earlier.

turns.speaker: Cirelle
turns.text: That explains the crowd; my own ride into Auness is 90 minutes on a good morning too.

notes.text: Cirelle's ride into Auness takes 90 minutes on a good morning.

turns.speaker: Eshven
turns.text: I tried the bike path to the alternate dock once, but the detour was still longer.

notes.text: Eshven tried the bike path to the alternate dock once, but the detour took longer.

turns.speaker: Cirelle
turns.text: Is the north dock any better?

turns.speaker: Eshven
turns.text: It's sheltered, but the ferry only stops at the north dock on every other departure.

notes.text: Eshven said the north dock is sheltered and the ferry stops at the north dock on every other departure.

turns.speaker: Cirelle
turns.text: I might try the 7:10 departure tomorrow if it has a seat; arriving late once beats freezing on the exposed ramp.

notes.text: Cirelle is considering the 7:10 departure tomorrow if a seat is available, because Cirelle would rather arrive late once than freeze on the exposed ramp.

turns.speaker: Eshven
turns.text: Fair. My hands froze last week just waiting for the ramp.

notes.text: Eshven's hands froze last week while Eshven waited for the ramp.

turns.speaker: Cirelle
turns.text: I asked dispatch this morning whether the morning bus connection can be held five minutes, and dispatch said they'd consider it.

notes.text: Cirelle asked dispatch this morning whether dispatch could hold the morning bus connection for five minutes, and dispatch said dispatch would consider the request.
